newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine farmers buy 15,000T Chinese yellow corn.
newsitem.headline: Philippine farmers buy 15,000T Chinese yellow corn.

text.p: The National Hog Farmers Association of the Philippines bought 15,000 tonnes of Chinese yellow corn at $138 to $140 per tonne C&F, Manila grains traders said on Monday.
Separately, Philippine poultry and feeds producer Vitarich Corp was looking for 8,000 tonnes of Chinese yellow corn for July arrival, they said.
The hog farmers bought the corn for July arrival, a member of the association told Reuters. Vitarich was also planning to buy Chinese corn for arrival in the country next month, traders said.
Philippine poultry and hog raisers are rushing to the import market for corn due to a local shortage and a drop in tariff on the commodity from 100 percent to 80 percent starting July 1.
The tariff cut on corn imports will be implemented as part of Manila's commitment to the World Trade Organisation.
The government allowed a lower tariff of 35 percent if corn was imported through the state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) but this was barred by a Philippine court early this month.
A group representing farmers and traders had protested against the lower tariff on commodities imported by the NFA, saying it discriminated against new entrants who could not use the NFA facility.
"But even at 80 percent tariff, imported corn will still come in cheaper compared to domestic corn," said one trader.
